speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node, which can sometimes indicate issues in the abdomen or chest. Have you experienced any recent changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea, constipation, or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any painless swelling of lymph nodes in other areas, such as your neck or armpits? I would also like to feel your abdomen to check for any enlarged organs.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: These symptoms are highly suggestive of lymphoma, so I need to confirm the presence of systemic involvement. REQUEST TEST: CT_Scan_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan confirms widespread lymphadenopathy, which strongly supports a diagnosis of lymphoma. To determine the specific type and guide treatment, I need to analyze the cells directly. REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index confirm a diagnosis of aggressive B-cell lymphoma, specifically Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
